unit.content: Area of a triangle using A=1/2 ab sin C; area of a triangle using Heron’s formula; area of quadrilaterals; area of regular and irregular polygons; application of area of polygons.
unit.coreCompetencies:
Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: the learner uses trigonometric ratios to generate the formula for the area of a triangle given two sides and an included angle.
Creativity and Imagination: the learner identifies shapes from the immediate environment that have the shapes of polygons and calculates their area.
Learning to Learn: the learner researches and discuss the use of polygons in real-life situations.
unit.values:
Patriotism: the learner uses the objects from the immediate environment and takes care of the environment.
Responsibility: the learner identifies objects in the immediate environment and takes care when calculating the area of regular polygons.
Peace: the learner harmoniously discusses and works in groups using trigonometric ratios to generate the formula for the area of a triangle given two sides and an included angle.
unit.pcis: Environmental Education: the learner collects objects from the immediate environment to be used as learning materials for the area of polygons.
unit.sep: Geometric construction, derivation, measurement and independent calculation.
unit.focus: Choose and justify an area method from verified dimensions; distinguish geometric calculation from field measurement.
unit.phenomenon: A fictional school garden has triangular and irregular beds. A tempting side-times-side estimate overstates how much covering is needed.
unit.supportingPhenomena: Labelled model diagrams, scale drawings and regular-polygon designs; no measurements are claimed to be from a real school.
unit.drivingQuestion: How can we defend a garden covering estimate? KICD: How do we work out the area of polygons? How do we apply the concept of the area of polygons in real-life situations?
unit.storylineThread: Height misconception -> sine derivation -> Heron -> scale -> quadrilaterals -> diagonals -> regular polygons -> heptagon/octagon -> irregular regions -> coordinate plan -> application -> assessment.

assessment.instructions: Time: 30 minutes within Lesson 12. Use C12 and show labelled sketches, formula choice, working and units. Scientific calculator allowed, in degree mode. Round the two regular-polygon areas to 1 decimal place. Other answers may be exact. Do not assume a sketch is drawn to scale.

sections.title: 1. Derive and apply
sections.prompt: For triangle A, show with a perpendicular height why A=ab sinθ/2 for the given acute included angle. Calculate its area.
sections.exemplar: Height=6 sin 30°=3 m if 8 m is the base. A=1/2×8×3=12 m². In general h=a sinθ, so A=bh/2=ab sinθ/2.

sections.title: 2. Three side lengths
sections.prompt: Find the area of triangle B and state why its side lengths form a valid triangle.
sections.exemplar: 5+5>6 and the other inequalities hold. s=8 m; A=√(8×3×3×2)=12 m².

sections.title: 3. A quadrilateral
sections.prompt: Find the area of trapezium C. Explain the role of its stated height.
sections.exemplar: A=(6+10)×3/2=24 m². Height is perpendicular distance between the parallel sides, not a sloping side.

sections.title: 4. Regular polygons
sections.prompt: For each polygon D, explain the congruent-triangle method and calculate area using the supplied apothem.
sections.exemplar: A=nsr/2. Heptagon 7×2×2.076521/2≈14.5 m². Octagon 8×2×2.414214/2≈19.3 m². Each centre triangle has base s and perpendicular height r.

sections.title: 5. An irregular region and a practical limit
sections.prompt: Find the area of E by subtraction and by a nonoverlapping decomposition. Explain one reason a real covering order could differ from this calculated area.
sections.exemplar: 9×7−3×2=57 m². A decomposition is 9×5+6×2=57 m². Real cutting waste, pack sizes or measurement uncertainty may change an order; accept another justified limitation.
